newsitem.title: PERU: Peru election body to rule on Fujimori third term.
newsitem.headline: Peru election body to rule on Fujimori third term.

text.p: The controversial debate over whether President Alberto Fujimori is entitled to run for a third term in 2000 will be settled by Peru's national election board, local media said on Saturday.
"The national election board will have the last say," Peruvian media quoted Ricardo Nugent, head of the Constitutional Court, the highest authority on constitutional matters, as saying.
Controversy has raged since Nugent's court issued a confusing double ruling on Thursday.

One declaration said a congressional ruling interpreting the constitution in such a way as to allow Fujimori to stand for re-election was "inapplicable." But a parallel declaration by the court said the first decision was "unfounded" due to the abstention of four of the court's seven magistrates, when six were needed for a majority.
Fujimori supporters interpreted the rulings as meaning he can run, while the opposition said it was clear he is barred.
Nugent did not specify when the election board would make its ruling to clarify the issue.

Under Peruvian law, a president who has been elected for two consecutive terms, as Fujimori's has, cannot run in the following election. But Congress in August voted in favour of the legal interpretation that meant Fujimori's first term would not be taken into account should he wish to stand for re-election.

Fujimori was elected president in 1990, and again in 1995 with 64 percent of the vote. After he dissolved parliament during his 1992 "self-coup," a new constitution was written the following year by a reformulated Congress, paving the way for the interpretation accepted in August.

The debate over Fujimori's possible re-election bid came as his faced the toughest test of his six years in office, with Marxist rebels holding 73 VIP hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima for the 32nd day.
The president has not formally announced an intention to run again in 2000, but has been quoted off the record by some close sources as saying that he wants to do so.
